But if the operating system is the only software on the computer, it can't really do much because all the operating system really is, as far as the user is concerned, is the interface between the user and the hardware...
That brings us to the next stage, the software which actually accomplishes the tasks that the computer is needed for - the application software.
Let's begin the lesson on APPLICATIONS....................................
LESSON MENU
APPLICATION SOFTWARE
DISCUSSION
An operating system is a software program designed to act as an interface between the computer's hardware and the application software.
A software application is a set of instructions for accomplishing a sequence of actions.

Bundled along with the operating system are a number of small applications which help provide additional functionality, but which are not really part of the actual operating system itself. This includes things such as a player for music CDs, a clock/calendar, etc...

As the interface between hardware and software, it is the operating system which is actually responsible for saving files, as an example.
The application software doesn't know how to talk to the disk drive, so instead it tells the operating system that the file should be saved.
The operating system presents a uniform interface so that all different kinds of applications can all save files (or perform other actions) in the same way.
It provides this same kind of uniformity for other functions
as well, such as telling the monitor how to display a graphic
or telling a modem whether it's supposed to be sending a
Application software falls into four general categories: productivity, communications, entertainment, and utilities.

Productivity software allows the user to produce and manipulate information in the form of words, numbers, or pictures. It includes word processing, database management, spreadsheet, graphics/multimedia, presentation, and education software...
Productivity software is the kind of software associated with offices,
Word processing is the manipulation of text. It includes everything from basic text editors to sophisticated desktop publishing (DTP) programs. A word processor is everything
that a basic typewriter is, plus a whole lot more.
Word processing applications come in two forms: text editors and full word processors.
CXQ`~ZHKTY

Text editors have minimal formatting capabilities. For example, font selection is the same throughout the whole document. A text editor will not allow part of a document to use one font and another part of the same document to use a different one...
A text editor includes a basic find (search) function, but it
doesn't support advanced features. In a full word processor,
for example, the find function may support searching for a particular color of text, not just a particular string of letters..
Also, a text editor only supports the most basic editing functions: undo, cut, copy, and paste.
In addition, tabs are preset at fixed intervals and are not adjustable.
Like the tab sets, margins are not adjustable..............
A text editor cannot have embedded graphics or other objects.

ASCII - the abbreviation for American Standard Code for Information Interchange. This is the agreed-upon standard for computers, so that a character typed on one computer will be interpreted as the same character on another computer...
DEFINITION

Note that few text editors are actually just text editors. Most are stripped-down word processors, which means that they have at least a few abilities more advanced than basic text editing. The particular functions will vary from program to program...
Word processors do basic editing, like text editors do, plus quite a few other functions as well.
BVVBVBVBVB
Where a text editor requires that all the text in a document be formatted the same, word processors allow separate formatting of each individual character in a document.

Word processors allow custom tab settings within a document. Not only can you set the tabs individually, you can even determine whether the tab will cause the text to align to the left, center, or right of the tab stop...
A word processor will also allow you to set the numbers of columns throughout the document and to control custom margins from section to section.

In addition, word processor documents can be divided into different sections by use of section breaks. This enables the use of headers and footers which can vary from section to section, keeping track of page numbers, chapter titles, and so on...
Another function that word processors can perform that text editors can't is linking to external databases for spell-checking, grammar check, etc.
L%%LLMMLLM
Word processors can also make use of macros for many different purposes such as automating tasks that are frequently repeated or are intricate and time consuming.

Another major innovation is the embedding of objects within a word processor document. This brings an entirely new dimension, literally, since one of the things that can be embedded is a link to another document or another place in the same document...
Desktop publishing brings the formatted text into a page layout context, giving more sophisticated control over the final appearance of the finished product.
In addition, DTP allows separate pieces (individual documents) to be compiled into a single integrated final document, giving much greater control to the publisher over the finished document...

Database management is the manipulation of data (whether as text, numbers, or images) which have been organized in some particular way..

The term "database" includes everything from a simple address book to the IRS's huge collection of taxpayer data. Customer lists are a common type, as are the lists of words which make up a spelling dictionary for a word processor.....
A typical example of a small database would be someone's personal address book.
A single piece of information is a field. For example, the entry in a field called NAME might be John Doe (or DOE in a field called LAST NAME, and JOHN in another field called FIRST NAME).

A collection of fields is a record. Things found in an address book might include a person's first name, last name, street address, city, state, zip code, telephone number, e-mail address, spouse's name, children's names, birthdays, and anniversaries...
Each of these would be an individual field, and all of them together would be a single record.

A collection of records makes up a database. There may only be a single record in a database or there may be millions. For instance, the internal revenue service maintains a database which includes separate records for every single taxpayer in the United States...
Asking for information from a database is known as a query. Finding, sorting, comparing, merging, and separating data
are all types of queries. The database responds to a query

Looking up Aunt Sally's birthday would be a query, as would be finding a list of all customers on the East Coast of the US who purchased a green Model XYZ widget with the advanced option package within the past 60 days...
Some databases are so simple that the user can figure out how to use them just by looking, and some are so sophisticated that it requires advanced training just to be able to ask the questions!
A spreadsheet is a program for the manipulation of numbers using mathematic or logic functions. It is meant for such things as bookkeeping tasks and other types of numerical analysis.
The construction of the spreadsheet is based on a kind of field called the cell. Cells are laid out in a grid of horizontal rows and vertical columns.

A range is a contiguous (adjoining) group of cells. It may be several cells in the same row, or it could be several cells in the same column, or it could a group encompassing several rows and columns at the same time..

But what exactly is a cell? Well, basically it is a container for either data (alphanumeric) or a formula or logic function. Data, formulas, or logic functions are entered into cells and results are automatically calculated and displayed...
Changing data in a cell causes the results of formulas involving that cell to be recalculated.
Charting and graphing can be done, based on values from a range of cells. Not only is this useful for financial purposes, it is also very useful for scientific and engineering purposes.
Graphics software is primarily concerned with the manipulation of images. It falls generally into two categories: bit-mapped graphics and vector-based graphics.
A bitmap directly controls the pixels, identifying the intensity and color of each individual pixel in order to create the picture on the screen.

Graphics of this type do not scale well, which is to say that trying to shrink or expand a picture distorts it, possibly to the point that it can't even be recognized. This is especially true of pictures which have been edited more than once...
This is because stretching out a bitmapped line also makes it thicker and more jagged.

Vector graphics, on the other hand, are a collection of mathematical descriptions of all the shapes that make up the picture. This means that to change the length of a line just means changing its length, not its thickness...

Multimedia is the integration of graphics and sound. Some PCs are described as multimedia systems, indicating a high degree of integration between sound and graphics, with sophisticated hardware for supporting each...
KPPKKPPKKP
Presentation software combines any and all other types of applications in order to disseminate information, possibly to more than one individual at a time, for briefings, training, and sales...
Presentations often use a multimedia approach to hold the audience's attention. Presentations are usually made in the form of slide shows or animations.
Educational software disseminates information in somewhat the same way that a real teacher does, but it has both advantages and disadvantages.

On the positive side, it is infinitely patient, where even the most patient of human teachers has limits to their patience. On the negative side, it is completely unable to address the issue of discipline...
KPPKKPPKKP

Software costs considerably less than a human teacher, but it is not adaptable the way that a human teacher is. When all is said and done, a human teacher can be more productive and can handle a larger number of students with the aid of software to take on some of the routine duties...

A variety of educational materials are available, including a great deal of software for teaching (especially for teaching children) in a sneaky way that makes it look like games and other entertainment...
This underhanded means of making people learn things without realizing that they are learning is sometimes called edutainment.

Software is also a very good way of teaching because it affords the student the chance to learn at an individual pace. There simply are not enough human teachers to enable all students to work 1-on-1, each at their own pace...

Communications software allows the user to transfer information from one location to another. It includes terminal emulation software (a.k.a. modem software), e-mail, web browsers, news readers, and file archive and retrieval software...

Communications software is the stuff that makes the internet and other networks possible. If the output of a computer couldn't be moved where it was needed, it would have a negative impact on the usefulness of the computer in the first place...
RRXNNEEJ
Entertainment software is primarily for enjoyment. It includes games, music, and multimedia.

Although it may seem trivial, one of the biggest driving forces behind the need for bigger/faster personal computers has been the need to provide higher-resolution, more realistic graphics for computer games...
Similarly, the quest for bigger/faster hard disk drives has been driven by the desire to archive more music and video clips.

Of course, there are more serious reasons for increasing performance, too. Businesses are keeping an increasing amount of their day-to-day operations on computers instead of on paper. But in the final analysis, it's entertainment that has opened up the home computer market...

It has been an extremely effective means of teaching children, and even adults are more susceptible to accidental learning when there is something to hold their interest.

Utilities are software which help hardware or other software run more efficiently or in a manner more to the user's liking,
but which don't actually produce tangible output such as text

Utilities include diagnostic and repair software, defragmentation software, anti-virus software, firewall software, and back-up software. It also includes things such as desktop themes, customized sound schemes, and so on...
Diagnostics and repair software keeps directories straight and fixes them when they become corrupted, so that the computer can locate files stored on disk.
DIRECTORIES - the files which a computer creates to keep track of the names of the files stored on a disk and the locations on the disk where those files are stored.
DEFINITION

Defragmentation software keeps the various pieces of files together so that the files load faster. When a computer works on a file and creates new data, it adds the new data to the end of the file. When it saves the changes, there may not be enough room for the whole file to be saved in the original location...

When that happens, the computer saves part of the file in the original location and saves the rest in other locations. The directory tells the computer where all the different pieces of the file are located...

It takes the computer much longer to locate and load all the pieces when they are scattered like that. Defragmenting a drive means collecting all the pieces together again, which speeds up the process of launching and running the software...

Anti-virus software keeps malicious software from causing problems. Most anti-virus software has two main components: a memory-resident program called a scanner, and the main program, called the console...

Firewall software is the other part of computer security.
Its primary purpose is to restrict remote access to a computer
in order to keep prying eyes off of personal data and to prevent malicious software which manages to gain access to the computer from being able to communicate without the user's knowledge.
It can usually be configured for different levels of security, allowing freer communication with computers located on a LAN, and more restricted communication with computers not on the LAN...
CCYCCYYCC

Back-up software gives you the ability to restore files that may become lost or damaged. Backing up critical files is one of the most important things that can be done, and is one of the most overlooked tasks on the computer...
The categories become more blurred as time goes on, with applications crossing the lines and incorporating features of applications from other categories of software into themselves.

For example, at one time a word processor did nothing except process text. Today, a word processor can include a complete movie file within itself, so that when the document is opened the user not only sees the words that have been placed on the page, but also can hear and watch an audio/video clip that has been embedded in the page.....
The document can also embed a part of a spreadsheet, so that a report can show data simultaneously represented as both columns of numbers and a chart depicting the data graphically.

Most word processors also include a mail merge function, which is more the province of a database, and many can also be used to send faxes. The spelling and grammar checkers that are considered an essential part of any word processor are types of databases...
Still, even though these cross-category capabilities exist, the primary purpose of a word processor is to manipulate text and the primary purpose of a spreadsheet is to manipulate numbers.
